turn.say: I got a new phone and NakhlaKey no longer works on it. How do I sign in now? I know SMS codes are not allowed any more.

turns.reply: If you have your old phone with NakhlaKey still installed, open Settings > Transfer on it and scan the code shown on your new phone to transfer your MFA device. If you no longer have the old phone but have your backup codes, sign in at https://id.nakhla.example/mfa using a backup code, remove the old device, and enrol your new phone. If you have neither the old phone nor backup codes, your manager must approve a reset after you verify your identity in person or by video call, and then Identity & Access Management will let you enrol again. Note that SMS codes are no longer allowed and cannot be used. If your phone was lost or stolen, report it immediately as a security incident. Backup codes are crucial for these situations, so keep them safe offline.

turn.say: My NakhlaID account showed NID-423 twice today and I don't know why. When do account lockouts have to be reported to Security Operations?

turns.reply: Your NakhlaID account locks after 5 failed sign-ins within 15 minutes, showing error NID-423. If you see three or more lockouts in one day without a known cause, this is treated as a possible password-guessing attack and must be reported to Security Operations. Repeated lockouts usually come from a device still trying an old password; update or remove the old password on all devices and then unlock your account.

turn.say: NakhlaID says NID-423 when I try to sign in. What should I do?

turns.reply: Your NakhlaID account is locked because of 5 failed sign-in attempts within 15 minutes, which causes the NID-423 error. The lockout lasts 30 minutes. To regain access, wait 30 minutes and then reset your password yourself at https://id.nakhla.example/reset by entering your work email and approving the NakhlaKey prompt or using backup codes. After resetting, sign out and back in on your devices. If you cannot reset your password yourself, an assisted reset requires a ticket, your manager's approval, and identity verification in person or by video call. Never share your password or codes with anyone.
